message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish a hand and by collecting cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each except one 0), plus two “Skip”, “Reverse”, and “Draw Two” cards. There are also four “Wild” and four “Wild Draw Four” cards. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a “Draw Two,” the first player draws two cards and loses their turn). | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a “Reverse” changes direction). On your turn you must play one card from your hand that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard card, or play a Wild card. If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction. (In a 2‑player game, it acts like a Skip.)
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Hand** | The first player to discard all of their cards wins the round. They receive points equal to the sum of the values of all cards still held by the other players: numbered cards = face value, action cards = 20 points, Wild cards = 50 points. | | **Scoring** | Add the round points to each player’s total. The first player to reach the agreed‑upon score (usually 500) wins the game. | | **Variations & House Rules** | • **Stacking** – Some players allow “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” cards to be stacked, forcing the next player to draw the cumulative total unless they can counter.
• **No “Wild Draw Four” challenge** – Some groups simply ignore the challenge rule.
• **“Skip” on the first card** – If the first card is a Skip, the first player is skipped.
• **“Reverse” on the first card** – In a 2‑player game, Reverse acts as Skip. | --- ### Quick Play‑through Example 1. **Deal**: 7 cards each. 2. **Start**: Flip top card – say it’s a Red 5. 3. **Player 1**: Has a Red 9 → plays it. 4. **Player 2**: Has a Yellow 9 → plays it. 5. **Player 3**: Has a Wild → plays it, chooses Green. 6. **Player 1**: Has a Green 2 → plays it. 7. **Player 2**: No green or 2 → draws a card. If it’s a Green 7, they play it. 8. **Player 3**: Plays a “Draw Two” (Green). Player 1 draws two cards and loses the turn. 9. **Continue** until someone discards all cards. --- ### Tips for New Players - **Keep track of colors** – If you’re low on a particular color, try to play a Wild to change the color to something you have more of. - **Watch the discard pile** – Knowing what cards have already been played can help you anticipate opponents’ moves. - **Use action cards strategically** – Save a “Draw Two” or “Reverse” for when you’re about to win or when you want to disrupt a strong opponent. - **Remember “UNO”** – It’s a simple rule but can save you from a nasty penalty. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
